items.summary: Targets are iid from a fixed distribution on[0,1] chosen at the beginning.
Knowing the distribution permits predicting its mean each round at expected cost sigma²T, with sigma² its variance.
We cannot do better than that.

Equivalently, consider the average.
Average expected excess, equation(1.2).
Both expected excess quantities are nonnegative.
Variance adjusts for the difficulty of the distribution; this is a reasonable but not sole metric.

source_gap_inventory.statement: The pages omit probability-space, measurability and integrability details needed to interpret expectations and random adaptive predictions. Unit-interval laws supply bounded-moment intuition, not a printed measure-theoretic proof.

No proof is printed that the population mean is in the action interval, attains the minimum of expected fixed-action cumulative loss, and has value T sigma^2. The expected-fixed minimum must be attained; no expectation/minimum interchange is licensed.

The assertion that no strategy beats the variance and the subsequent nonnegativity assertion have no printed argument. The missing bridge must account for prediction before revelation, dependence on past observations, and the randomization model if one is added. Mere target IID does not make an arbitrary random prediction independent of the current target.

The finite positive-horizon division identity and the equivalence of sublinear cumulative excess with average excess tending to zero are asserted, without an explicit proof. A finite lower bound alone supplies no successful strategy or convergence.

The contextual pathwise squared-loss minimum is written without an attainment argument. It is a different object from minimum expected fixed loss; it is used already in the definition display, not only its later interpretation.

extension_obligation_inventory.statement: Produce joint seed-plus-past/current independence from independence of S and the whole target process and joint independence of target coordinates. Coordinatewise seed/target independence alone is insufficient.

Establish the generated sigma-field containment/monotonicity and transfer independence to variables measurable in each subordinate F_t. Do not assume prediction-current independence as a theorem premise.
Establish measurability of the finite history map and jointly measurable tape/history policy composition in G_t. Separate measurability alone must not silently replace joint measurability.

From ambient measurability and almost-sure unit-interval feasibility, derive finite second moments and integrability for predictions, targets, squares and products required by the identity. No completion or AE-measurable factorization theorem is supplied by the source.

Prove the one-round square expansion with vanishing mixed term using the produced current independence, then finite-sum expectation and the expected-fixed benchmark. Prove the sum is nonnegative. The source does not print this identity.

Show that finitely many almost-sure target support events give a legal strict history almost surely, and use policy feasibility on that cube for every seed. This supplies feasibility of the actual prediction; arbitrary off-cube values are not source behavior.
